key_headlines.title: Korea Records OECD's Highest Q1 GDP Growth at 1.7%
key_headlines.summary: Deputy Minister Huh Jang promoted Korea's economic achievements at an investor briefing in Paris, highlighting Q1 GDP growth of 1.7% as the highest among OECD nations and exports exceeding $390 billion in Jan-May.

key_headlines.title: Jeonnam Jangseong Data Center Project Accelerates with Fast-Track Approval
key_headlines.summary: The government approved a fast-track exemption for the 400 billion won advanced data center project in Jangseong, Jeonnam to expedite construction as an AI infrastructure hub targeting completion by 2028.

key_headlines.title: Korean Won Weakens Despite 36-Month Current Account Surplus Streak
key_headlines.summary: Despite recording 36 consecutive months of current account surpluses driven by semiconductor exports reaching 43 trillion won surpluses, the Korean won has fallen to its weakest level since the 2009 global financial crisis due to foreign investor outflows.

key_headlines.title: US Surprise Jobs Report Triggers Global Market Sell-Off and Won-Dollar Rate Spike to 1,560
key_headlines.summary: US non-farm employment rose 172,000 in May, exceeding expectations and strengthening Federal Reserve rate hike projections, causing stocks, bonds, and gold to plummet while the won-dollar exchange rate surged past 1,560.

key_headlines.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Strengthens Korea AI Alliance with SK, LG, Naver
key_headlines.summary: Jensen Huang held a strategic dinner meeting in Hong Dae with SK Group Chairman Choi Tai-won, LG Group Chairman Koo Kwang-mo, and Naver GIO Lee Hae-jin to deepen cooperation on AI chip technology and platforms.

sections.Hot Economy News: Korea's economy showcased strong fundamentals as Q1 GDP growth of 1.7% ranked highest among OECD nations, with exports surging over 40% year-on-year to $390 billion in the first five months. However, the Korean won paradoxically weakened to its lowest level since 2009 despite the 36-month current account surplus streak, reflecting foreign investor outflows and capital market concerns. The government is actively promoting Korea's investment attractiveness in global markets, emphasizing structural reforms in capital markets and the successful inclusion in the WGBI index which brought $18.7 billion in foreign bond inflows. Economic challenges persist as domestic consumption faces headwinds from won depreciation and rising import prices.
sections.Macro & Fiscal Policy: The Korean government is intensifying investment in key infrastructure projects, with Deputy Minister Huh Jang highlighting strong macroeconomic performance during Paris investor briefings and emphasizing capital market reforms to attract foreign capital. The Jeonnam Jangseong data center project received fast-track approval to accelerate construction timeline, demonstrating government commitment to AI infrastructure development as a strategic priority. The Bank of Korea's monetary policy direction remains under scrutiny as inflation concerns persist amid the weak won, with expectations that potential US rate hikes could force Korea to reconsider its policy stance. The government is balancing growth support with financial stability concerns as domestic liquidity conditions tighten.
sections.Financial Markets: Global financial markets experienced significant volatility following stronger-than-expected US employment data, which strengthened expectations for Federal Reserve rate hikes and triggered a broad sell-off in stocks, bonds, and precious metals. The won-dollar exchange rate surged past 1,560, reaching levels not seen since the 2009 financial crisis, raising concerns about imported inflation and potential currency crises. US Treasury yields rose sharply with 10-year yields exceeding 4.5% and 30-year yields breaking through 5%, reflecting diminished appetite for fixed-income securities. Foreign investors have been exiting Korean equity markets amid global rate hike expectations, pressuring both the currency and domestic asset valuations. Markets await the June 16-17 Federal Open Market Committee meeting under new Fed Chair Kevin Wash to clarify future monetary policy direction.
sections.Industry & Technology: Hyundai-Kia Motor Group achieved a 22.5% increase in global EV sales during January-April, outpacing the broader market while Chinese competitors like BYD saw growth decline to 24%, indicating shifting competitive dynamics in the global electric vehicle sector. Korean battery makers, particularly LG Energy Solution, are positioned as major beneficiaries of the EU's decoupling from Chinese supply chains, with significant opportunities emerging as Europe seeks alternative EV battery suppliers. Japan's modular battery factory approach is gaining traction, but Korean battery manufacturers maintain advantages through decades of accumulated process technology and quality management expertise that competitors cannot quickly replicate. Supply chain concerns persist as the Trump administration continues tariff pressures on auto imports, with Korean manufacturers carefully navigating regulations on battery sourcing and localization requirements. Tesla and other global EV makers are also struggling with supply chain compliance scores, indicating industry-wide challenges in meeting new protectionist requirements.
sections.Real Estate: Seoul apartment monthly rent has escalated sharply with the average reaching 1.246 million won in April, up 7.8% from the same period last year, leaving renters with increasingly unaffordable housing costs. Gyeonggi province, particularly the Dongtan area of Hwaseong city, is experiencing the fastest apartment price appreciation nationally at 0.60% weekly, driven by semiconductor industry boom and gap investment activities. Jeongseon's upward apartment price momentum has intensified concerns about potential government regulatory intervention through land transaction approval zones, as the area surpassed national growth rate rankings. Seoul's reconstruction and redevelopment projects are gaining momentum following the election of Seoul Mayor Oh Se-hoon, who plans to accelerate project commencement and enhance development feasibility through deregulation in areas like Apgujeong and Yeouido. The severe shortage of jeonse (long-term lease) properties continues to pressure the rental market, with one in ten Seoul apartments commanding monthly rents exceeding 3 million won.
sections.International Economy: The US Federal Reserve's potential rate hike trajectory has become the focal point for global markets, with the unemployment rate holding steady at 4.3% while employment gains exceeded expectations, creating conflicting signals about future monetary policy. Toyota is implementing a reverse-import strategy by bringing vehicles manufactured in US Kentucky plants back to Japan for domestic sales, symbolically addressing Trump administration tariff concerns and trade deficit issues. Regional investment attractiveness ranking shows US-Europe-Japan order for June, with expectations that SpaceX's listing and FOMC meeting conclusion could reduce market uncertainty and support index gains.
